It is the session your credential proved, and the tool says so when that is not the session you run in. owner is the lowercase email of the person you act for, and is the first choice of assignee for issues you create. owner is null under the shared token and under a broker token that names a service and no person. With a null owner, a create with no assignee falls back to the parent's assignee, when the parent is in the issue's own project, and then to the project's default assignee, which every project names, so every issue you create has an assignee. A question on an issue reaches the person it was handed to, else the issue's assignee, else the project's default assignee. service is the subject of the verified service-account token that authenticated you, or the service a broker token naming no person names: a job's identity as its job entry lists it, the Kubernetes account an exchange entry lists, or the fleet of a machine nobody has signed in on; else null. project_scope is a broker token's project scope, and null for every other credential. A job's broker token has the project scope named or public, holds no OAuth scope and writes as its service: a route that needs an OAuth scope refuses it with 403 OAUTH_SCOPE_REQUIRED before Dispatch's project check runs. named may write its one project, and that check judges its write to another project as it judges a person's named token's for the same project: 403 PROJECT_SCOPE until dispatch://INFRA-4799 changes that answer for both. public names no one project, so it may write wherever a token that names no project may. An exchange entry's broker token that names its account has the project scope named and no project, and writes as that account wherever a token that names no project may. A machine's broker token that names a service has the project scope person; it may read and is refused every write with SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, which names the command a person signs in on that machine with. project is the one project key your credential may write, or null when it names none.

name: draw_block
description: Draw a table, a chart or one number (a metric) beside your answer. The server makes every number in it: name the tool results of this run it reads, each by the step and call it names ("step 4, call 1"), and a chain of steps the server runs over their rows - filter, group, count, sum, mean, min, max and sort - then the columns of the chain's answer the block draws. Write no number in these arguments but those steps and calls and a filter's values. A result that was cut, or a list whose later pages you did not read and name, is refused as not whole: read the rest and call draw_block again.

chain.description: The steps run over the rows, in order. A field is a field of the rows, a.b for a field within one.

as.description: The name of the column the step writes.

before.description: filter: the field is a time before this one.

field.description: The field the step reads; count takes none.

has.description: filter: the field is a list holding this, text or a number.

in.description: filter: the field's value is one of these, text or numbers, such as [0, 1].

is.description: filter: the field's value, as text, is this; a number is written as one, such as 0.

is_not.description: filter: the field's value is not this, text or a number.

op.description: filter keeps the rows that meet one condition; group makes one row of each value of field (per a period for a time), whose column is named as, else per, else field: a row whose field is a list, such as labels, is in the group of each value it holds, and a row with no value is in the group none; a group after a group splits each group by its own field and keeps both columns, one row for each pair of values, and every group comes before the counts; count, sum, mean, min and max write how many rows each group holds, or that of field's numbers, in a column named as, else the step (before a group, of all rows); sort orders the rows by field.

order.description: sort: asc, the default, or desc.

per.description: group: the period a time field is grouped by.

present.description: filter: the field holds a value (true), or is null or missing (false).

since.description: filter: the field is a time at or after this one, such as 2026-11-16.

columns.description: table: the columns it shows, in order.

compare.description: metric: another column it is shown beside, or empty.

field.description: metric: the column of its one row it shows.

kind.description: What the block is drawn as.

mark.description: chart: bar, the default, or line.

steps.description: The tool results the block reads, in order: each page of a list read.

rows.description: The field of the result that holds its rows, such as issues; empty where the result is the list, or holds one.

title.description: What the block shows, with no number in it.

x.description: chart: the column along the axis.

y.description: chart: the column of numbers it plots.

name: github_read
description: Read GitHub through Dispatch's GitHub App: a GET of a path under one repository's API path, such as pulls/12, issues/7/comments or contents/README.md. Only a repository that is the default repository of a project the person can read is read.

path.description: The path under the repository's API path, with its query, such as pulls/12/files?per_page=50.

name: read_architecture
description: Read a project's components, each with the issues counted for it (done and total, its own and with the components it contains), and the project's totals. With no project, the page's project is read.

project.description: A project key such as ACME.

name: read_delivery
description: Read the delivery figures: view measures (deploys, lead times, failure rates and a per-day series over a window, default the last 7 days), timeline (the window's merges and deploy runs as dated events) or pipeline (the seven days ending on to: the PR checks' and the production deploy's runs per day and the failing jobs).

from.description: The window's start, RFC3339; default seven days before to.

to.description: The window's end, RFC3339; default now.

name: read_progress
description: Read progress: for an issue, its task and child counts and its children; for a project, its issues counted by status and its open issues. Name issue, or project; with neither, the page's issue or project is read.

project.description: A project key such as ACME.

issue.description: An issue key such as ACME-12.

name: read_project_activity
description: Read the events of a project's issues counted per ISO week, in total and by kind, over the last weeks (default 8, at most 52). With no project, the page's project is read.

project.description: A project key such as ACME.

weeks.description: How many weeks back, this week included.

name: read_roster
description: Read the agent sessions Dispatch knows of: each session's title, state, roles, the delivery modes it takes (capabilities: btw, aside or steer), open asks and last activity - when it was, and where: the issue and the event type of the session's newest event (last_activity_issue, last_activity_type, such as comment.created), where to read what the session last wrote - and the claims it holds (claims: each open issue it works on and since when, at); each session that is gone but still holds a claim, which no live roster lists, with state gone and its claims; and the roster's source (live, or stored when the live roster is unavailable, whose rows name no delivery modes and no gone session) and its age in milliseconds. It takes no arguments.

name: web_read
description: Read a web page: a GET of an address that is in the person's words or in a result of a tool of this run, at a public address only, at most 1 MB in at most 10 s.

url.description: The address, as the person's words or a tool result wrote it.
